title: DevForgeAI worker result
description: The receipt: the single JSON object a phase worker returns as its final message on either provider. It carries no file bodies and no hashes. A producer has already written its files inside the candidate root; a judge has written nothing anywhere and returns its evidence in `findings`, which the sequencer persists. The sequencer validates this object at the identity-bearing SubagentStop event, diffs the candidate root against the input checkpoint to derive what actually changed, runs the transition oracle inside the root, checkpoints, and advances, retries, or rewinds.

run.description: The active run id. Story runs use the story id; document runs use '<skill>-<arg>'. Must equal run.yaml#run.

skill.description: The active skill, or one of its variants. 'dev-tdd' resolves to 'dev'.

agent.description: The canonical worker name, or a registered alias. Must resolve to the same canonical name as the stop event's agent_type; the model-supplied value is never identity.

status.description: Closed worker status vocabulary. gate_policy values are never returned here.

reason_code.description: Required when status is could_not_run; rejected with any other status. provider_tool_refused means the provider refused a tool call before any DevForgeAI hook ran. hook_fault is reserved for two causes only: a hook event that lacked identity, and a malformed receipt. prerequisite_missing: a project prerequisite for the candidate mode (git HEAD, ignored work dir, tracked settings or stack.yaml) is absent, sequencer-synthesised at phase start. checkpoint_fault: the sequencer could not take or diff a checkpoint, sequencer-synthesised at ingest.

candidate.description: Which candidate root the worker worked in, and which checkpoint it started from. Required on every status, because a judge that read a checkpoint must name the one it read.

id.description: The candidate id, which is the run id. Must equal run.yaml#run.

input_checkpoint.description: The checkpoint this phase started from: 'base', or the name of the phase whose checkpoint it read. Must equal run.yaml#candidate.checkpoint at dispatch.

claimed_paths.description: Every path the worker believes it created, edited or deleted inside the candidate root, root-relative. Empty on any status other than pass, and always empty from a judge, which holds no write tool at all. The sequencer derives the truth from the checkpoint diff and refuses the receipt when the derived change set is not a subset of this list (UNCLAIMED_CHANGE). That subset check runs only on status pass: a producer that edited and then failed claims nothing by rule and has changed something in fact, so on a non-pass status the diff is recorded as changed_unchecked and no fence, policy or oracle check runs over it.

evidence_refs.description: Paths to evidence the sequencer should read: a report inside the candidate root, or an oracle output the sequencer already wrote under .devforgeai/work/<run>/. A report-producing phase names its report here, and the report's own frontmatter carries the verdict that selects the handoff row. A judge names no findings path here: it returns its evidence in `findings`, and the sequencer, not the worker, chooses the path that string is persisted to. Never a file body.

note.description: At most three lines of plain summary. Rendered into <phase>-report.md.

findings.description: The judge's detailed evidence, as prose. Required when the phase's worker is a judge (the registry writes mode for the active phase is none) and the status is pass or fail; optional on a judge's needs_user or could_not_run; forbidden on a producer receipt. At most 16384 UTF-8 bytes; maxLength here bounds code points, and the sequencer enforces the byte bound. The sequencer never truncates it: an oversize findings refuses the receipt like any other defect. At ingest the sequencer writes the decoded string verbatim to .devforgeai/work/<run>/evidence/<agent>/findings.md, records that path as findings_path in <phase>-result.json, and references it from the handoff; the next phase's worker reads it by path. issues[] stays the bounded routing summary of at most 10 rows. This string enters the primary context as part of the subagent's returned result, which is why it is bounded.

issues.description: One-line findings. Not a repair instruction and not a status.

next.description: A rewind request naming an earlier phase of the same skill. Legal only with status fail, only from a phase that declares rewind_to, and only when it equals that phase's rewind_to. The sequencer rewinds the candidate root to the checkpoint the named phase started from - its predecessor's, or base when it is the first phase - and re-enters it, because the named phase's own output is what is being redone.

path.description: A POSIX path relative to the candidate root, or to the project root for an evidence path under .devforgeai/work/<run>/. Must resolve inside the root it is relative to.
